summary.headline: CSL Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 2% YoY to Rs 19.4 crore while SME retail stalled; wholesale carried growth and FY26 PAT rose 19% to Rs 86 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 showed a split performance: wholesale kept growing on AUM, asset quality and profitability, while SME retail lagged amid industry consolidation and new competition in the sub-Rs 10 lakh secured segment. AUM reached Rs 1,448 crore (up 21% YoY) with the mix now 69% wholesale and 31% SME retail. Q4 PAT of Rs 19.4 crore was up 2% YoY but down 7% QoQ on higher ECL provisions and write-offs, and Gross NPA rose to 1.1%. Management guided to 15-25% AUM growth for FY27 and expects SME retail to normalise gradually.

financial_highlights.change: +21% YoY from Rs 1,195 crore at start of year
vs 0.46% Q4 FY25 and 1% Q3 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Net worth / book value per share

financial_highlights.change: consistent across all quarters of FY26

segments.name: Wholesale
segments.commentary: Now 69% of AUM and described as the key growth driver; management cites strong collections over the last two quarters and no current stress on newly boarded accounts. Off-book co-lending deals were closed in Q4 to build fee income.

segments.name: SME retail
segments.commentary: Now 31% of AUM, down from a peak of 48% in FY23-24; growth has been weak for 12-15 months. Ticket focus is Rs 7-50 lakh after exiting the Rs 10 lakh segment, and the company is consolidating low-productivity branches.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guided at 15%-25%, in line with the last 3-4 years.
Management expects SME retail to return to normalcy in FY27 but has not given SME growth numbers; next 2-3 months are a cautious re-observation of policies.
Credit cost, which was around 0.5%, is expected to stabilise at that level; management does not expect absolute gross or net NPAs to rise in FY27.
Effective tax rate for FY27 expected at around 27% weighted average versus the 25.17% normal rate, due to Ind AS fee amortisation.
Branch expansion to resume from Q3 FY27; operating expenses expected to fall with branch consolidation and team rationalisation.
Co-lending and joint lending to grow fee income in FY27 and beyond.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 44 branches across 7 states; spoke locations continue to be added, with some converting to branches.
Net branch additions were nil during the year as branches were reshuffled and relocated.
Management plans to focus on productivity of existing branches for the next 3 months before resuming openings from Q3 FY27.
No geographic expansion beyond current region planned for the next 12-15 months due to limited funds.
demand_pricing: SME retail hit by over-leveraged borrowers in the lowest income strata, stagnant MSME incomes, and new aggressive lenders (formerly MFI-heavy) in sub-Rs 10 lakh secured SME lending.
Management attributes SME slowdown to senior team changes, higher branch attrition, tighter policies and geopolitical caution.
Wholesale co-lending: sole lending for tickets up to roughly Rs 30-40 crore; co-lenders brought in for larger tickets, with the company retaining 10%-15% to 40% stake.
Wholesale focus is the daily NCR market, a niche where management says ample opportunity exists.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 disbursements fall 16% QoQ and what is the FY27 disbursement outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wholesale is lumpy and should be judged annually; Q4 was lower after an elevated Q3, and prepayments and collections affected the number. No absolute disbursement guidance was given beyond AUM growth of 15-25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new ECL framework?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board approved a new ECL policy this quarter, more objective and based on 4-5 years of SME portfolio performance, per RBI direction. Management said it would have produced a lower provision than the current conservative approach, so no adverse impact is expected from FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the higher tax rate in Q4 and what is FY27 tax expected to be?
qa_highlights.answer: Ind AS fee amortisation creates a gap versus income-tax computation; the weighted average effective tax rate is expected around 27% versus the 25.17% normal rate.

qa_highlights.question: How does the co-lending / off-book strategy work and what is the ticket split?
qa_highlights.answer: Co-lending earns processing and other fees, with no risk sharing as in DA. Sole lending up to about Rs 30-40 crore; co-lenders are onboarded for larger tickets to manage risk and cash flows.

qa_highlights.question: Why has SME share fallen and what is the strategy to rebuild it?
qa_highlights.answer: SME share fell from a 48% peak in FY23-24 to 31%. Causes cited: senior team changes, branch attrition, tighter policies, and a cautious stance over the last 3-4 months. Strategy is to source only better-CIBIL customers, consolidate branches, and re-observe policies for 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost and NPA outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost around 0.5% is expected to stabilise. Management said the recent NPAs came from large SME tickets of Rs 50 lakh to Rs 1.5 crore that were stopped; SARFAESI resolutions should offset fresh slippages.

risks_watch: SME retail recovery depends on macro improvement; management has not provided SME growth numbers and is in a cautious phase for 2-3 months.
Gross NPA rose to 1.1% from 1% in Q3 FY26; watch whether resolutions via SARFAESI bring it down as guided.
Wholesale asset quality is untested in a stressed cycle; RBI standard provisioning on project finance rose to an average of 0.98% from 0.8%.
Co-lending fee income is a new revenue stream whose scale is not quantified.
Q4 disbursement and AUM trajectory is lumpy, and Q4 FY27 AUM growth could be flat if the 15-25% guidance is not met.
summary.management_tone: Confident on wholesale and co-lending, cautiously optimistic on SME retail. Management gave few hard numbers on SME and repeatedly deferred projections to later quarters.
key_quotes: While wholesale has continued to grow from strength to strength, supported by AUM growth, asset quality and profitability, SME retail performance has been underwhelming.
Growth is expected in the SME retail book in FY27 as well and we expect to do better as the operating environment becomes more conducive.
The next year guidance will be in line with anything between 15%-25% that we have been doing it for last 3-4 years.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 AUM growth of 15-25% (midpoint 20%) with no SME growth numbers, and branch expansion resuming only from Q3 FY27 with nil net additions in FY26, so backing is vague and relies on wholesale co-lending and a normalising SME book.
